chunks: 1021 - And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man does not know whether he has prayed two, three, or four [rakʿahs], so he said:
He should pray two rakʿahs standing, then perform salām, then pray two rakʿahs while sitting.

key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives the salām concluding the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he does not know whether he prayed two, three, or four rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes uncertain in salat (prayer) whether he has prayed two, three, or four rakʿahs. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to perform two rakʿahs standing, then give salām, then perform two rakʿahs while seated, indicating a prescribed way to address doubt in prayer.
